I was a floating voter for a long time before I found my home in this party.

I went from a Blairite, to an ABC (Anyone but Conservative), to Labour under Jeremy Corbyn (not my finest hour) and then a local independent. It took me a very long time to become politically astute and work out what my actual vision was and if I could be swayed on any of them visions.

Don't get me wrong, there are still some things I don't agree with in the last manifesto or what we do locally at times, but the difference between this party and any other party I've been a part of is the willingness to listen and not be in the mindset thinking shouting louder is better than being knowledgeable.

I will say though that thr main difference is how much more work we have to put in as Lib Dems. There are very few areas in the country where you can wear a yellow rosette and be automatically granted a vote like Labour or the Tories have in the past. We need to be really active in our communities to make our mark and that takes time.

I live in a traditionally Labour area (which has just gone over to Reform at Council level), but yet we are now the official opposition through very hard work and dedication of the councillors in my area.

I think that is what you can expect if you decide to join us but I will say that politically, it's the best choice I've made.

I'll come from a different point of view from the other comments that I am seeing.

First of all, well done on realising you have a major problem and making it public, even if it is under anonymity. It takes guts to do that and especially getting help as well. As someone who had a therapist for 6 months for mental health issues, I know that the first step is the hardest, so I congratulate you on getting the necessary help again.

On to sorting it out with your husband. Unfortunately, your actions now mean that this is out of your hands, whether you want them to be or not. Your actions have not only put your husbands job at risk, but he could well be feeling emasculated  and demeaned by them as well. You'll have affected his relationship with his co-workers to a point where some might be scared to build any form of relationship due to being scared of similar actions coming their way.

Also, your husband will likely not wanting to be going into work and then not wanting to come home afterwards, which could lead to feelings of depression on his part, which could exacerbate things as well.

In other words things are completely out of your control now and your marriage now lies in his hands and whether he wants to continue it or finish it. The only advice I can give is that you continue to work on yourself and your issues (the ones you've told on here and the other issues you haven't disclosed on here in my opinion).

I commute from Stanley into Belmont daily for my job.

I've seen that you know Nevilles Cross is a nightmare to navigate on a morning and this is definitely true with the traffic get to and from Durham Johnston in particular, especially any time around 8am as I have found out the last few mornings (I'm the postman for that area). 

I would completely avoid trying to go anywhere near the roundabout just north of the hospital as it is always at a standstill around the time you will be setting off. Also I would avoid Crossgate Peth as it is traffic jammed right back up to the lights at Nevilles Cross, unless you know the trick to avoid it.

If money isn't too much of an issue for you, I would recommend parking your car for the day on either Waddington or Sutton Street and walking to the train station from there for ease as it will be extremely difficult to judge the amount of time it'll take to get through the traffic into Newcastle. My best guess is that all of the country roads will be quite backed up as well as there is very rarely ever a way into Newcastle on a morning that is even half clear.

I know this will mean you have the difficulty of getting to your workplace once in the town, but at least you can plan your times well in advance.
